description: Ground-truth benchmark dataset for Hybrid RAG retrieval, reranking, and generation evaluation.

questions.question: What is the vector dimension generated by the embedding model?
questions.expected_answer: The sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model maps input text into a 384-dimensional dense vector space.
questions.notes: Ground truth verified on Page 1 of technical specification.

questions.question: What are the default HNSW construction parameters M and efConstruction in ChromaDB?
questions.expected_answer: The default HNSW construction parameters use M=16 bidirectional links per node and efConstruction=100 search depth during construction.
questions.notes: Exact parameters M=16, efConstruction=100 verified on Page 1.

questions.question: What are the parameter values for k1 and b used in the BM25 scoring function?
questions.expected_answer: The parameter k1 is configured to 1.5 to control term frequency saturation, and b is configured to 0.75 for document length penalization.
questions.notes: BM25 parameters k1=1.5 and b=0.75 verified across both documents.

questions.question: Why does the pipeline avoid normalizing raw retrieval scores before combining candidate lists?
questions.expected_answer: Reciprocal Rank Fusion eliminates the need to normalize raw cosine distances and BM25 scores onto a shared numerical scale, avoiding calibration distortion caused by unbounded score distributions.
questions.notes: Semantic explanation on rank aggregation advantages on Page 3.

questions.question: How does the cross-encoder attention mechanism differ from bi-encoder retrieval?
questions.expected_answer: Bi-encoders process queries and documents independently for fast search, while the BGE cross-encoder performs full all-to-all self-attention across every query token and document token simultaneously to capture fine-grained token-level cross-interactions.
questions.notes: Detailed architectural distinction between bi-encoder and cross-encoder on Page 4.

questions.question: What decoding temperature and maximum output token limit are configured for Gemini generation?
questions.expected_answer: The decoding temperature is set to a deterministic 0.2 with a maximum output limit of 1024 tokens.

questions.question: How do BM25 lexical search and BGE cross-encoder reranking work together in the hybrid pipeline?
questions.expected_answer: BM25 provides sparse token matching from an inverted index, RRF fuses lexical candidates with dense vector candidates, and the BAAI/bge-reranker-base cross-encoder evaluates joint sequence pairs using full all-to-all attention to reorder documents by calibrated sigmoid relevance probabilities.
questions.notes: Synthesizes lexical retrieval (p2), RRF fusion (p3), and reranking (p4).

questions.question: What mathematical formulas are used for Reciprocal Rank Fusion and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain?
questions.expected_answer: RRF scores chunks using RRF(d) = sum(1 / (k + rank_m(d))) with smoothing constant k=60 (Page 3), while nDCG@K evaluates graded rankings using a logarithmic position discount log2(rank + 1) divided by ideal DCG (Page 6).
questions.notes: Spans RRF math on Page 3 and nDCG formula on Page 6.

questions.question: How are dense vector lookups and BM25 index storage implemented to avoid security risks and achieve low latency?
questions.expected_answer: ChromaDB constructs persistent HNSW graphs for fast sub-linear cosine vector lookups (Page 1), while BM25 stores raw chunk metadata in JSON format to guarantee deterministic index reconstruction without relying on insecure Python pickling (Page 2).
questions.notes: Connects ChromaDB HNSW (Page 1) and secure BM25 JSON persistence (Page 2).
